data.title: Clipboard Hijacking (Crypto-Clipper)
data.summary: The sample monitors the clipboard for content matching a cryptocurrency address pattern and silently replaces it with an operator-controlled address, redirecting the next paste.
data.description:
This relies entirely on a user not re-checking a pasted address character-by-character
before confirming a transaction — a reasonable assumption given how unwieldy wallet
addresses are to read. The monitoring itself is lightweight (a clipboard-format change
notification or a polling loop checking GetClipboardData against a set of regular
expressions for different coin address formats) and runs continuously in the background
with no other visible activity.
data.recommendation:
* Verify the destination address against a trusted source (QR code, address book entry) immediately before confirming any cryptocurrency transaction, rather than trusting a pasted value.
* Hunt for processes registering clipboard-format change notifications or polling the clipboard API persistently with no corresponding UI.
* Recover the regular-expression address patterns used; they indicate which cryptocurrencies the sample specifically targets.
data.short_recommendation: Verify any pasted cryptocurrency address against a trusted source before confirming a transaction.

mitre_techniques.procedure: Polled the clipboard for content matching Bitcoin and Ethereum address regular expressions and replaced matches with an operator-controlled address.

mbc_techniques.implementation: Clipboard monitor replaced address-pattern matches with an operator-controlled address before the next paste.
